stem: Ishaan wets a cotton handkerchief and places it on his forehead on a hot afternoon. As the water disappears, his forehead feels cooler. He also thinks about water vapour in the air and about simply wetting the cloth.

parts.text: Why does his forehead feel cooler as the water disappears?

options.text: Evaporation of the water takes heat from the skin.
Water vapour condenses into water on the skin, and this condensation cools the skin.
Wetting the handkerchief cools the forehead even if none of the water evaporates.
The water evaporates because the skin becomes cooler.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Evaporation produces a cooling effect on the nearby skin as water changes to vapour and heat leaves the surface.

teacher.key_rationale: Evaporation cools the remaining surface. Condensation is the opposite process. Wetting alone without evaporation does not explain the cooling as the water disappears. Cooling does not cause the evaporation here.
